subject: Discovery recap + single question: are we moving forward or pausing?
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Recap] Discovery notes + suggested next steps

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so your team has a single view and a suggested next step. If I missed anything, I can update and resend.

Key takeaways:
- BrightLane is evaluating a single inference endpoint to replace two in-house models for customer support triage (avg payload ~450 tokens).
- Primary constraints: 95th percentile latency < 300ms, GDPR data localization for EU users (pilot scope: US-only), and a tight budget window for Q3 POC.
- Success criteria for POC: 10% FTE reduction in manual tagging + parity in intent accuracy within 2% of current model.

Suggested next steps (pick one):
1) 2-week POC on Redwood Hosted with a 10k-message sample (we'll provide an ops playbook and instrumentation)
2) Dedicated trial (reserved pool) — if you need consistent throughput and want to validate latency at scale
3) Pause and revisit next quarter — we’ll keep this on our radar and check back in August

Attachments: discovery-notes-20270510.pdf (PDF, 42KB), initial-sow-outline.docx (DOCX, 18KB)

If you’re open to option (1) I can send a short SOW and 3 calendar slots for a kickoff next week.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

If it helps, we can limit the POC to a single queue and target a 7-business-day technical validation before expanding. Happy to sync for 15 minutes — three slots below:

- Tue May 25, 09:00–09:15 PT

If none of those work, tell me a good window and I’ll handle scheduling.

Thanks for the quick reply — even a one-line priority signal helps us know whether to engage engineering.
